verdict.rationale: BugSnag ships its own iOS and Android SDKs: a hands-on community report says the iOS library auto-reports fatal errors, and the docs cite iOS app-hang capture, device-correlated events and release filtering. However, NDK/native C/C++ crash capture is never mentioned, and device, OS and app-version context on crash events is only implied. Missing for 10: any NDK crash-capture evidence, explicit Android crash-capture docs, documented device/OS/app-version metadata attached to crash events.

support.subject: As a developer, I can capture native mobile crashes — iOS, Android, NDK — with the device, OS, and app-version context needed to reproduce them

citations.quote: The iOS library had a nice interface, would take minutes to add, and auto-reports fatal errors.
The new appHangCallback in the BugSnag iOS SDK lets you add diagnostic context, such as the current screen or how many assets are still loading, the moment an app hang is detected.
Instantly see related BugSnag events sharing the same user, device, session, or trace
filter your dashboard by release and identify which release errors were introduced in.
